claims.text: Mechanical-property differences among equiatomic FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni-based alloys are governed partly by local lattice distortion quantified by MSAD.
Greater MSAD raises the extrapolated 0 K CRSS through enhanced solid-solution strengthening.
At high temperatures, dynamic elastic solute pinning provides an additional strengthening increment.
Mn and Fe are the predominant solutes responsible for high-temperature dynamic pinning.
Dynamic solute pinning produces Portevin-Le Chatelier-type serrated flow through a Cottrell-type mechanism.
The proposed specimens are homogenized, water-quenched equiatomic FCC single crystals comprising the quinary alloy and its quaternary and ternary derivatives.
The proposed specimens are grown by Bridgman or optical floating-zone methods and annealed for 168 h at 1273 or 1473 K.
Compression along the [1̄23] orientation can be used to determine CRSS for (111)[1̄01] slip in these crystals.
The controlled investigation spans 9–1373 K at an engineering strain rate of 1 × 10^-4 s^-1 and includes strain-rate jumps during Stage I deformation.
Data below each alloy's inertial-critical temperature should be excluded from thermally activated analysis.
The PL effect begins above 873 K.
Cr-containing alloys have larger local lattice distortions than non-Cr-containing variants.
Below room temperature, deformation is dominated by thermally activated dislocation glide hindered by lattice-distortion-derived solid-solution obstacles.
Between approximately 673 and 973 K, dynamic solute pinning causes a modest CRSS increase and serrated flow.
Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, higher-MSAD alloys, particularly Cr-containing alloys, will have higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS.
Relative to the equiatomic quinary baseline, alloys richer in Mn and Fe will have larger high-temperature CRSS increments and more pronounced serrated flow.
Cooling below room temperature substantially increases CRSS.
Below approximately 77 K, inertial effects make the temperature-dependent rise in CRSS less steep.
Heating into the diffusion-active regime produces modest strengthening relative to room temperature.
Failure of higher MSAD to correlate with higher extrapolated 0 K CRSS, or failure of Mn and Fe content to correlate with high-temperature strengthening and serrations, would reject the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that the PL effect begins above 873 K, whereas the mechanism places dynamic pinning and serrated flow over approximately 673–973 K.

The conditions specify exclusion of points above 873 K, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule require evaluation of high-temperature CRSS increments and PL serrations, while the experiment extends to 1373 K. It is unclear which high-temperature data are admissible for testing the hypothesis.

The hypothesis treats dynamic solute pinning as one of the governing mechanisms, but the boundary limits validity to the regime before dynamic solute pinning becomes dominant, leaving the stated scope of the high-temperature mechanism ambiguous.
